Tests get a small, fixed set of named agents, each with a hard daily cost cap. If a cap is hit the test fails on purpose: the guard works, and a bad loop cannot run up a bill.

## Run it

```bash
make dev-infra   # Postgres + Redis + MinIO (once)
make run-api     # control-plane on :8080 (terminal 1)

export PAL_E2E_API_URL=http://localhost:8080
make test-e2e    # terminal 2
```

The target runs `make e2e-lint`, then the `e2e/runtime`, `e2e/quickstart`, `e2e/examples` and `e2e/deploy` suites (Go, build tag `e2e`, standalone modules, so plain `go test ./...` never runs them). `make test-e2e-llm` is an alias. It targets the single-tier topology (stub scheduler, no KVM needed). Quickstart needs an LLM provider configured for the dev tenant.

On a two-tier stack (`PAL_SCHEDULER_GRPC_ADDR` plus a Docker-backend runtime-manager) set `PAL_E2E_IMAGE_DIGEST` to a locally pullable image; with the placeholder default, schedule returns 500.

## Suites

| Dir | Covers |
| --- | --- |
| `e2e/runtime` | `/v1/runtime/*` control path: auth gates, schedule (201 + vm_id), tenant-scoped list, detail and audit, logs SSE, terminate, quota 402. |
| `e2e/examples` | The fixture-tier example flows (digest, Telegram, voice); see [Example suites on a fixture stack](#example-suites-on-a-fixture-stack). Needs the fixture stack that `make test-e2e-examples` builds. |
| `e2e/deploy` | The deploy CLI against a control-plane (the `deploy-cli` CI job). |
| `e2e/quickstart` | The `examples/quickstart/` agents: create from `spec.json`, post `run.json`, poll to `succeeded`, assert an output shape; incident-summarizer also issues and verifies a receipt. Real LLM calls. |

## Spend policy

Enforced by `e2e/internal/e2ekit`, which is the only way a suite creates agents or posts runs:

- Agent names must be one of 8 reserved names: `e2e-quickstart`, `e2e-support`, `e2e-pr-triage`, `e2e-incident`, `e2e-digest`, `e2e-analyst`, `e2e-assistant`, `e2e-voice`. At most 8 `e2e-*` agents exist at once.
- Each agent gets a hard-fail budget before any run: `maxCostUsdPerDay` 0.50, `maxRunsPerDay` 15, `hardFail` true. The kit reads it back and fails the test if it is absent.
- Model is pinned to the cheapest tier: `reasoning-small` if Anthropic is configured, else `chat-small`, else `fast` (env-configured keys). Never a large model.
- `web_search` is stripped from every spec except `e2e-assistant`.
- A `402` on `POST /v1/runs` fails the test with `e2e daily budget exhausted for <name> (cap working; rerun after local midnight)`.
- `make e2e-lint` fails the build if anything under `e2e/` references `/v1/budgets/tenant`; the tests never touch the tenant-wide cap.

The quickstart suite posts 3 runs per invocation against one slot, and the cap is 15 runs/day, so expect about 5 full runs per day. The pinned model is the agent's `model`, so runs try the cheapest tier first; the budget is still what bounds spend.

## Environment variables

| Variable | Default | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `PAL_E2E_API_URL` | `http://localhost:8080` | Target API. Canonical; always set it explicitly. |
| `PAL_API_URL` | unset | Alias, used only when the canonical var is unset |
| `PAL_E2E_EMAIL` | `admin@pal.dev` | Login email (seeded dev user) |
| `PAL_E2E_PASSWORD` | `pal` | Login password |
| `PAL_E2E_IMAGE_DIGEST` | placeholder digest | Image to schedule in the runtime suite; needed on two-tier stacks |
| `E2E_ALLOW_SKIP` | unset | `1` turns a down stack into a skip |

The runtime suite prints the resolved target URL at the start of a run.

### E2E_ALLOW_SKIP

Every test probes `GET /healthz` first. If the stack is unreachable the test **fails**, so `make test-e2e` exits non-zero and you know nothing ran. With `E2E_ALLOW_SKIP=1` it skips and exits 0. A reachable API with wrong credentials is always a failure.

```bash
E2E_ALLOW_SKIP=1 make test-e2e   # exits 0 when the stack is down
```

## What it creates

- Agents named from the reserved `e2e-*` set above, each with a budget.
- Runs on those agents (quickstart), and scheduled VMs plus a temporary quota row (runtime).

Tests delete their agents via `t.Cleanup`, and the runtime suite terminates its VMs and restores the quota row even when assertions fail. The quickstart suite also sweeps leftover `e2e-*` agents in `TestMain` before running.

## make e2e-clean

Manual recovery after an interrupted run. It runs `go run ./cmd/sweep` in `e2e/internal/e2ekit`, logs in with the same URL and credentials variables, lists `GET /v1/agents`, and issues `DELETE /v1/agents/{name}` for every agent whose name starts with `e2e-`. Nothing else is deleted; failures are printed, never fatal. Use it when the kit refuses to create an agent because 8 `e2e-*` agents already exist.

```bash
PAL_E2E_API_URL=http://localhost:8080 make e2e-clean
```

## Browser tier (Playwright)

`apps/web/e2e` drives the real dashboard in headless Chromium: sign-up, forgot/reset password (the reset link is read from the log mailer), onboarding (template gallery and the free-text path through the fixture LLM to a succeeded first run), the settings danger zone, and the light/dark theme.

```bash
cd apps/web
npm ci && npx playwright install chromium
npm run test:e2e
```

It boots its own stack on spare ports (web 3411, API 8411, llm-replay 9412): a throwaway Postgres database, a private Redis db index, the control-plane (with `PAL_CORS_ORIGINS` set to the dashboard origin), llm-replay and `next dev`. It never touches :8080, :3001 or the shared `pal` database, and tears everything down afterwards. Needs Go, `psql`, and Postgres and Redis reachable (the `make dev-infra` defaults work; override with `E2E_PG_ADMIN_URL`, `E2E_REDIS_*`). Details and kiosk-spec hooks: `apps/web/e2e/README.md`.

## CI

`.github/workflows/sdlc-e2e.yml` runs the fixture tier on every pull request and push to master, with Postgres (pgvector) and Redis service containers and no provider key. Three jobs: `examples` (`scripts/e2e-examples.sh`), `browser` (Playwright; report and traces are uploaded on failure) and `deploy-cli` (`e2e/deploy` against a control-plane started in the job). There is no skip path: a skipped test fails the job. The real-LLM suites (`make test-e2e-llm`) are a local gate only, because they need a provider key and spend money.

<Aside type="danger">
Never point the suites at a stack with real tenant data: they delete every agent named `e2e-*` in the logged-in tenant.
</Aside>

## Fixture LLM tier

**What.** `llm-replay` is a small stdlib server that speaks the OpenAI chat-completions and Anthropic messages wire formats (JSON and SSE streaming, text and tool calls). Setting `PAL_LLM_BASEURL_OPENAI` and/or `PAL_LLM_BASEURL_ANTHROPIC` sends every control-plane provider call there instead of the real API.

**Why.** CI and kiosk mode need the same answer every time and must not need a provider key or spend money. Token usage is still reported, so budgets and cost metering run for real.

**How.** The default reply is `fixture: ` plus the first 60 characters of the last user message. A rules file scripts the rest; the first rule whose `match` is a substring of the system prompt or the last user message wins (this is how the demo kiosk tells its agents apart). `GET /healthz` returns 200.

```json
[
  {"match": "refund", "reply": "Refund issued."},
  {"match": "weather", "tool": {"name": "get_weather", "args": {"city": "Austin"}}}
]
```

A `tool` rule fires only when the request declares tools. When the next request carries the tool result, the reply is `fixture: tool result: <first 60 chars>`, so a scripted tool loop always ends. Usage is about one token per 4 characters of the request body and the reply.

### Try it

```bash
cd services/control-plane
go run ./cmd/llm-replay -rules rules.json      # 127.0.0.1:9192

PAL_LLM_BASEURL_OPENAI=http://127.0.0.1:9192 \
PAL_LLM_BASEURL_ANTHROPIC=http://127.0.0.1:9192 \
OPENAI_API_KEY=dummy make run-api

curl -s localhost:8080/v1/completions -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -d '{"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"hello"}]}'   # "fixture: hello"
curl -s 127.0.0.1:9192/__requests                         # what the control-plane sent
```

### Limits

- Dev and test only. The control-plane refuses to start with either variable set when `PAL_ENV` is prod, production or staging, and ignores them at request time.
- A provider key must still exist (database or `OPENAI_API_KEY`/`ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`); any dummy value works.
- Only `/v1/chat/completions` and `/v1/messages` are served. Other provider endpoints (embeddings, speech, transcription) return 404.
- No model quality: it echoes and follows rules. It cannot validate prompts.

## Example suites on a fixture stack

**What.** `make test-e2e-examples` runs `scripts/e2e-examples.sh`: it creates a throwaway database, starts `llm-replay`, `connector-replay`, the control-plane (pointed at both) and the surface-gateway, runs `e2e/examples`, and tears everything down. It never touches `:8080` or your dev database. Needs Postgres and Redis from `make dev-infra` (a random Redis DB 1-14 is used).

**What it asserts.**

| Test | Flow |
| --- | --- |
| `TestDigest_*` | Schedule with `America/New_York` returns a 09:00 New York `nextFireAt`; made due, the scheduler creates the run; GitHub is read and exactly one multi-line `chat.postMessage` reaches the Slack fixture with the digest intact; the schedule advances to the next 09:00. A bad timezone is a 400. |
| `TestTelegram_*` | Missing or wrong `X-Telegram-Bot-Api-Secret-Token` is a 401 and sends nothing; a signed update runs the workflow (Google Calendar fixture read) and a `sendMessage` with the answer reaches the Telegram fixture for the right chat; a second message gets its own reply. WhatsApp `X-Hub-Signature-256` negatives live in `services/surface-gateway/tests`. |
| `TestVoice_*` | Unsigned and wrong-token webhooks and status callbacks are 403 and change nothing; a signed inbound call gets TwiML and reserves $0.05 in `agent_usage_daily`; the status callback (61 s) reconciles it to $0.06, replays are no-ops, a never-connected call refunds to zero; over a hard-fail budget the call gets `<Reject/>` with no row and no spend. |

**Try it.**

```bash
make dev-infra
make test-e2e-examples                 # ~70 s, mostly the scheduler's 60 s poll

E2E_EXAMPLES_SERVE=1 scripts/e2e-examples.sh   # leave the stack up, no tests (debugging)
scripts/e2e-examples.sh -run TestVoice          # extra args go to go test
```

**Limits.**

- Connector and LLM replies are recorded fixtures; this proves the wiring and the security gates, not model quality or vendor API drift. Real-account runs are in each example's README.
- The gateway creates runs over gRPC, which the control-plane's recovery sweep drives; the script sets `PAL_RECOVERY_INTERVAL=2s` so a reply takes seconds, not up to 30.
- Needs `go`, `cargo`, `psql`/`createdb` and `python3` on the PATH. Runs in CI as the `examples` job.

## Not covered

- True cross-tenant isolation (a second tenant probing the first) needs a second seeded tenant.
- `PUT /v1/runtime/quota` clamps non-positive ceilings, so the 402 test pins `maxConcurrentVms` to the current live-VM count instead.
